wu_song_mengzhou:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: production game sprite animation atlas, not concept art. Create ONE TRANSPARENT RGBA PNG sprite sheet for a 2D isometric RTS Water Margin campaign. Character is Wu Song at Mengzhou before becoming a Buddhist traveller: tall powerfully built adult Chinese man, knotted black cloth headwrap, dark blue-grey plain cloth tunic and loose trousers, beige cloth waist sash and calf wraps, cloth shoes, clean broad face, EMPTY HANDS. No swords, staff, necklace, monk robes or armor. Hand-painted realistic game illustration, restrained earthy palette, crisp silhouette, softly shaded cloth; orthographic 2:1 isometric game camera, no baked ground shadow.
Exact composition: 8 columns by 10 rows, all 80 cells uniform square, entire canvas ideally 2048x2560. Invisible regular grid, no grid lines, NO text, labels, numbers, border or background. Every complete figure wholly inside own cell with generous transparent padding. Center at x=50% of cell, ground/sole anchor at y=82% for standing poses; no sprite bleeding into another cell.
Layout uses five 2-row blocks. Rows 1-2 = idle breathing four frames. Rows 3-4 = walking four distinct cycle frames. Rows 5-6 = empty-handed punch attack four frames wind-up, punch, full extension, recovery. Rows 7-8 = recoil/hurt four frames. Rows 9-10 = non-gory defeated/down four frames from stagger to seated collapse, lowest ground contact stays y=82%.
For EACH two-row block: odd row columns 1-4 face SOUTH-EAST (front three-quarter towards screen lower right); odd row columns 5-8 face SOUTH-WEST (front three-quarter towards screen lower left). Even row columns 1-4 face NORTH-EAST (back three-quarter towards screen upper right); even row columns 5-8 face NORTH-WEST (back three-quarter towards screen upper left). These are FOUR genuinely drawn views of the same consistent character: back views show back of headwrap and back of tunic, front views show chest and face. Do not mirror a front view for back view. Keep body scale, cloth colors, headwrap and camera completely consistent across the 80 frames. Transparent means actual alpha=0 background, not white, grey, checkerboard or colored matte.
